parsed.doc_summary: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12 (Tenant Protection Act rent cap, as re-enacted by SB 567): 5% + CPI, max 10%, operative 2024-04-01, repealed 2030-01-01. Yields to stricter local rent control; exempts new construction (15 years), deed-restricted housing, etc.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act rent cap
rules.requirement: Owners may not raise rent more than 5% plus the local CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, in any 12-month period, with at most two increments. Initial rent on a new tenancy is not capped.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
rules.effective_date_note: Current version operative April 1, 2024 (effective Jan 1, 2024); the cap originally applied to rent increases on or after March 15, 2019 (AB 1482).
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing; dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (not mobilehomes); certain separately alienable properties (single-family homes, condos) with non-corporate/non-REIT owners and written notice; owner-occupied duplexes; mobilehome homeowners.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property generally, unless exempt.
rules.interaction: Does not apply where local rent control restricts annual increases to less than the state cap; does not expand or limit local authority under Civ. Code ch. 2.7 (§ 1954.50 et seq.).
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive relief, actual damages, attorney's fees, and up to 3x damages if willful; enforceable by the Attorney General, city attorney or county counsel.

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes and condos owned by non-corporate, non-REIT owners with written notice
